body:
CANDIDATE bd-01M162YNC4QQ2VKWQZQJZMFD9V (the de-escalated P3): 3aa29e0 on m1/relpres, stacked on my pending 1c75de1. Two files, align only. This closes out my own retracted finding honestly: the consequence claim was wrong, the defect in kind was real, and it turned out to have two siblings I had not seen.

WHAT WAS THERE. diagnostic() returned 1.0 for a layer the recall stated no relations of - "every recalled relation is preserved" said about a recall that claimed none. Inside it, two more of the same kind that my original report missed entirely: (a) a relation whose ENDPOINTS CARRY NO SOURCE MASS scored 0.0, so units we could not place read as evidence that the participant's stated ordering was violated; (b) a SIMULTANEOUS claim scored 0.0, though a claim that two things happened at the same time states no ordering to preserve or violate - it is not evaluable as a world-time ordering at all.

(b) is the one I would flag to the interview and scoring owners as a pattern rather than an instance: a relation type that is CATEGORICALLY not evaluable by a given metric is different from one that is evaluable and failed. Scoring it zero is not conservative, it is wrong in kind, and it will always push the aggregate one way.

SHAPE: LayerPreservation(mean: Option[Double], evaluated: Int, stated: Int) per layer. I deliberately did NOT collapse to a bare Option. "You stated no relations of this layer" and "none of the three you stated could be evaluated" are different facts and the second is the more informative one; a bare None loses it. The support is therefore always present, and the mean is the thing that abstains.

MUTATION PROOFS, three, each applied alone and reverted - and the third needed a new fixture, which is the fourth time tonight an unreachable branch has hidden behind a green suite: R1 restore the 1.0 default, 2 tests FAIL. R2 score an unplaceable pair 0.0, 1 FAILS. R3 score a Simultaneous relation 0.0 SURVIVED at first, because AnnaFixture states no simultaneity - I added a recall that does, and it FAILS properly. I am no longer surprised by this; I now assume a surviving mutant means my corpus cannot reach the branch until I have proved otherwise.

EVIDENCE at 3aa29e0, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 152/152, alignJS 152/152 (was 149), lawsJVM 81/81, fixturesJVM 108/108, embedBench 44/44, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green.

I also wrote the call-graph fact into the Scaladoc - that this is a diagnostic and reweight is the production path - with a note that I once claimed otherwise on the board and the call graph disagreed. The next person to read this function should not have to re-derive what I got wrong.

Stack order for landing: 1c75de1 (second-review rework), then 3aa29e0.
